blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY— Marinduque residents, environmental advocates and members of the faith community gathered on Monday at the provincial capitol here to urge the Department of Environment and Natural Resources to release the “communication” needed to finalize the $100-million Marcopper mine disaster settlement with Barrick Mining Corp. In 2006, Barrick acquired the Canadian company that used to run Marcopper Mining Corporation, which polluted Marinduque waterways and potable water after a tailings storage leak unleashed toxic waste that required years of cleanup. The March 1996 accident released about 1.6 million cubic meters of mine tailings into the Makulapnit-Boac River system. READ: Barrick Gold […]...
